title: Barrowlight
intro:
Rain has followed you for three days across the Greywater moor. The villagers of Hollin's Rest would not say the barrow's name. They only pointed north and made the sign of the ash.

Somewhere beneath that mound lies the Barrowlight, the lantern the Ashen Order kept burning so their dead would sleep. It went dark at the turn of the season. Since then, the graves of Hollin's Rest have not stayed shut.

You crest the last hill as dusk bleeds out of the sky, and the lichgate rises before you.

epilogues.text:
The Seal of the Waxing Moon and the Seal of the Unclouded Sun sink into their sockets with a sound like two bells struck a world apart, and the Bronze Gate of the Twin Seals begins, at last, to grind open.

Sister Wren stands at your shoulder with the Barrowlight's gold on her face. Behind you, by the Wayfarers' brazier, Prelate Vaelen sits with Lira's silent carillon in her lap and does not wind it, and Commander Silas is chalking his garrison's names back onto the crossroads wall, one by one, beginning with his brother's. Neither of them is healed. Both of them are still here, and they chose to be.

Below the gate, a stair older than the Order winds down toward the Cradle of the First Architect, the one who first taught Greywater to fear its dead. The lantern burns steady and warm. "Whatever waits down there," Wren says quietly, "it has never met anyone who let go and stayed." You take the first step together, {player.name}.

Moon and sun turn together in the bronze, and the Gate of the Twin Seals groans open on a stair that breathes cold, ancient air.

You spared the Prelate and you spared the Commander, and the Memory Warrens are quieter for it. In the Archive, Lira's carillon has finally run down, and Vaelen let it. In the Iron Reliquary, the lye vats stand cold, and Silas says Tomas's name aloud now and then, haltingly, like a man learning to walk again. Neither faction will thank you. Both will remember that someone came down the stair and listened.

The Barrowlight warms in your hand as you descend toward the Cradle of the First Architect. You go alone, {player.name}, but not unwitnessed.

The Moon Seal settles into the gate as gently as a child laid down to sleep. The Sun Seal goes in still hot from the Furnace of Remission, and still marked by the fight it took to win it.

In the Archive, Prelate Vaelen has let her daughter's carillon fall silent at last. In the Iron Reliquary, the garrison stands leaderless around Commander Silas's broken plate, not knowing whether to scour their names again or to remember them. You gave grief room to end, and gave iron nothing but iron. The Barrowlight burns uncertain between gold and ash, as if it cannot decide which of those things you are.

The Bronze Gate grinds open toward the Cradle of the First Architect. Down there, {player.name}, the one who first chose order over mourning is waiting to ask which of your two answers you meant.

You set the Sun Seal first, taken from a commander who laid down his glaive and remembered his brother. The Moon Seal goes in second, cold in your hand, pried from a carillon whose keeper you could not reach.

In the Iron Reliquary, Silas's soldiers are chalking their own names onto their blank iron masks. In the Archive, the Hollow Choir has stopped every music box in mourning for its Prelate, and the silence there is not peace. You could bear the soldier's grief and not the mother's. The Barrowlight burns in two colors at once, warm on one side and frost-pale on the other.

The Bronze Gate grinds open toward the Cradle of the First Architect, {player.name}. Whatever waits below will know exactly which griefs you were willing to hear.

The seals go into the bronze still marked by what it cost to take them, and the Gate of the Twin Seals opens with a shriek like iron being scoured.

Behind you, the Memory Warrens have gone silent. The Choir's music boxes have stopped and the Reliquary's furnace has gone out, and between them no one is left who will say your name kindly. Prelate Vaelen and Commander Silas each held a piece of the old balance, and you took both pieces by force. The Barrowlight burns frost-white in your fist, giving light and no warmth at all.

You descend toward the Cradle of the First Architect alone, {player.name}. Down there waits the one who first decided that the dead must be made to obey. You may find you have more in common than you would like.

Moon and sun, the Triad Seals turn in their sockets, and the Bronze Gate of the Twin Seals grinds open on a stair that winds down into older dark.

You leave the Memory Warrens changed, if not settled. The Archive and the Reliquary will each tell the story of your passing differently, and neither will be entirely wrong. The Barrowlight's flame wavers as you step onto the stair, neither gold nor ash, waiting to be told what it is.

Below lies the Cradle of the First Architect, {player.name}, and the last question the Under-Barrow has to ask.

gameOverText: The cold of the barrow closes over you like deep water. Somewhere far above, rain falls on the lichgate, and the Barrowlight stays dark. Your story ends here, {player.name}.
